description: The no-till seeder machinery has been developed to support Morocco's national plan of having one million hectares of farming land under Conservation Agriculture practices by 2030 (Generation Green 2020-2030). Developed from a local prototype by an ICARDA, INRA and local manufacturer team, using technology imported from dryland farming machinery in Australia, the no-till (zero tillage) seeder allows smallholder farmers in Morocco to sow seeds directly into the soil (direct seed) without causing any mechanical modification of the soil structure. No-till practices are expected to improve the resilience of dryland smallholder farmers by reducing soil erosion and increasing the amount of carbon dioxide, water, and organic matter retained in the soil.

description: The on-farm Water, Energy, Food, and Carbon footprint (WEFC) nexus index has been developed to enable the quantitative assessment of on-farm integrated resources management in wheat and faba bean farming systems in Egypt. The WEFC index is computed as the weighted arithmetic average of the four pillars of (1) water: on-farm saved water consumption/national maximum water consumption; (2) energy: on-farm saved energy consumption/national maximum energy consumption; (3) food: on-farm agricultural yield/national maximum yield; and (4) carbon dioxide (CO2): on-farm saved CO2 emissions/national maximum CO2 emissions. The WEFC nexus index values are, therefore, indicative of resource consumption (inputs) and agricultural production and CO2 emissions (outputs). The index can be used to quantitatively assess the nexus performance of site-specific packages of practices under certain conditions and quantify the impact of new interventions on the nexus status to drive transformative actions at the farm level.

description: The Agroecology initiative aims to contribute to achieving agroecological transition through developing and scaling a range of innovations in 8 countries across three continents. It proposes to do so by using a participatory action-research approach involving the key stakeholders of the Agroecological Living Landscapes (ALLs), multi-stakeholder territorial spaces in each country on which the Initiative targets its transformation and innovation efforts. A major pillar of such an approach consists in codesigning the required innovations and corresponding processes as well as effecting the required changes in behavior/practices by the concerned actors. At the heart of the initiative’s ambition and approach lies the ability to mobilize and support ALL stakeholders in co-designing and implementing the diverse activities required to develop the innovations needed in each context. Hence, the initiative has designed a tool to support this process.

description: The RVF tool is a collaborative effort between the One Health Initiative and the Digital Innovation Initiative, designed to analyze climate-epidemic interactions and support decision-making for Rift Valley Fever (RVF) outbreak prevention and control in the Greater Horn of Africa. It includes a decision-support system for managing RVF epizootics, enabling timely and effective responses, and integrates a disease information management system for efficient data compilation and dissemination. The tool enhances disease surveillance in high-risk areas by combining trapping systems with community reports and supports cost-effectiveness studies on RVF prevention strategies, informing contingency planning. It provides meteorological data, including rainfall and precipitation at county and sub-county levels, and incorporates RVF modeling for risk assessment. Additionally, it serves as a key resource for prevention and control efforts, featuring an online news bulletin that enables users to generate customized scientific advisories with geospatial visualizations and professional reports.

description: Climate adaptation processes can be uneven and reinforce inequitable power relations and outcomes. In dairy households of Nandi and Bomet counties in Kenya, despite women’s significant labor contributions, gender norms limit women’s access to resources and decision-making agency. Rather than top-down, one-size-fits-all solutions, adaptation must prioritize flexible, locally led approaches tailored to diverse capacities of households and groups with differential access to resources and opportunities. Our innovation combines two inclusive approaches, scaling with households and champions in groups to enhance women's capacities to learn, lead and scale adaptation. The first approach works with households as part of the Pioneer Positive Deviance (P-PD) approach to scale farmer-led solutions developed by “adaptation pioneer households” (APHs). The second approach works with local champions and grassroots women-led groups to support women's peer learning in collectives and strengthen their leadership capacities. Synergies between these two piloted approaches support equitable scaling of locally led adaptation.
title: Scaling with households and groups: socially inclusive approaches supporting equitable scaling of locally led adaptation in Kenya's dairy sector

description: This innovation is a new/adapted technology for conservation of Suidae (pig) genetic resources in-vitro based on a stem cell approach.The technology relies of harvesting of somatic cells (such as from an animal’s body), which are then bought back to undifferentiated stem cells, also called induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), in the laboratory. The iPSCs can be stored in-vitro (under liquid nitrogen) and later used to produce any cell type (undifferentiated stem cells are characterized by their ability to produce any cell type in the body). To date we have successfully demonstrated stable lines of local pig somatic cells in culture. The steps in progress include inducing pluripotency, characterizing and demonstrating their differentiation potential, and later using them in assisted reproductive technologies to revive the pig which cells were stored in liquid nitrogen. This technology will be used to conserve tropical pig genetic resources in Uganda, Vietnam, and potentially elsewhere.

description: The Climate Security Programming Dashboard for Climate Finance (CSPDxCF) is a comprehensive tool designed for initial conflict sensitive assessments and guidance for projects funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF) along with other climate funds and financial institutions. In the project design phase, CSPD assists Accredited Entities (AEs) and Direct Entities (DEs) in identifying operational risks and entry points for peace-informed action, providing tailored guidance on integrating climate strategies with security programming. Additionally, CSPD enhances AEs and DEs due diligence and risk management, optimizing project design in fragile and conflict-affected settings.

description: In response to  rangeland degradation, conventional practices involving exotic species like Acacia saligna and Atriplex nummularia have exacerbated ecological imbalances by endangering local flora and fauna and diminishing biodiversity. While developing the Tunisian National Strategy for Advancing Feed and Forage Resources in Tunisia, ICARDA proposed innovative solutions centered on the reintroduction of indigenous species. These were carefully selected to thrive in specific agroecological zones addressing key constraints, and which will be implemented by the Office of Livestock and Pastures and other national institutions. Drivers of loss of indigenous species planting include limited seed availability, lack of awareness, and entrenched institutional behavior. Therefore, our strategies involve genetic source scanning to match indigenous species with environmental conditions, raising awareness about indigenous species' benefits, and efforts to change institutional behavior. Additionally, we are exploring ways to enhance seed collection and multiplication. This approach revitalizes degraded rangelands, contributing significantly to climate change mitigation.

description:
Targeting Tools is a web-based Geospatial Information System (GIS) platform that houses a wide range of spatial datasets, both global and country-specific. It provides Land Similarity, Land Suitability, and Land Statistics tools for use on both desktop and web platforms._x000D_
The platform not only facilitates the visualization of datasets stored in its geodatabase but also supports user-uploaded raster format datasets. It enables various types of suitability or risk mapping analyses by combining different datasets._x000D_
Users are given the flexibility to establish their own criteria and thresholds to identify suitable areas. Moreover, these tools can be used to characterise the identified areas through the calculation of zonal statistics.  _x000D_
The tool allows for the integration of multi-dimensional datasets, including bio-physical (e.g. climate, soils, agro-ecology) as well as socio-economic (e.g. poverty, nutritional status, access to markets) data and thus for analyses along the different CGIAR impact areas.

description: The Climate Security Observatory (CSO) is an online decision-making support tool providing robust, localized, and policy-relevant evidence on	how	exactly climate security risks	may	emerge across different geographic contexts. It aims to answer several	research	questions on how the  climate security nexus operates at the subnational level. To achieve this , the CSO performs a series of mixed-methods analyses (data-driven literature review, pathway analysis, social media issue mapping, governance coherence analysis, network analysis, spatial analysis, econometric analysis), before synthesizing outputs into an open-access online dashboard. Within the CSO, a module for decision making on displacement-related is being developed.

description: Pig and beef cattle keepers in Son La province of NorthWest Vietnam rarely engage in best practice in pig and beef cattle production and marketing. description: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is designed for Excellence in Agronomy (EiA) Use Case teams with an interest in developing gender- and youth-responsive agronomic solutions. The SOP is a guide to help Use Case teams move from each step in their workflows when designing, validating, and piloting their Minimum Viable Products (MVPs) to ensure they can develop gender- and youth-responsive agronomic solutions by the end of their Use Case. This stepwise procedure first entails carrying out a diagnostic assessment of gender and generational differences in agricultural management practices and technology adoption and the factors contributing to these differences. These steps (6 total) to developing gender- and youth-responsive agronomic solutions are described with some detail in this SOP. The SOP has been used during the implementation of the integrated survey to ground the Use Cases. Reports from 3 Use cases are shown in the evidence.

description: Accurate measurement of crop cultivated area is essential for assessing various agronomic gain key performance indicators (KPIs) including yield, profitability, and resource use efficiency. Previous household surveys heavily relied on farmer-reported plot area. However, it has been reported frequently that farmer-reported plot area is often biased due to various reasons. Here, we describe procedure for a GPS-based field area measurement. Module 1 introduces the use of GPS devices as first option, whereas module 2 describes the use of application software on smartphones and tablets as second option. Here, we describe UTM Area Measure, an android application downloadable for free from Google Play Store, as an example. This module describes the procedures for downloading and performing the measurements with this application. There are many other applications, that have functions similar to those of UTM Area Measure. They can also be used to measure field/plot area

description: We develop a novel approach for spatial analysis based on databases characterizing sub-national units in various countries using Uber H3 level-6 hexagons—a spatial grid system. Uber's H3 system optimizes spatial data exploration, enhancing geographic information analysis across various data types: crops, livestock, population, and climate. Unique identifiers in H3 hexagons aid data aggregation, outperforming square pixels for broad spatial coverage. Note: Hexagon size may differ from actual pixels like SPAM; values vary by location and underlying pixels. Interpret as important indicators, not absolute values. Our database serves researchers, policymakers, and organizations keen on foresight analysis. We actively promote H3 system integration into existing models, offering documentation, tutorials, and support. Preliminary appraisals ensure system accuracy and reliability. This innovation provides invaluable insights using efficient spatial data analysis for foresight purposes, benefiting stakeholders.

description: The Climate Smart Governance (CSG) Dashboard provides accurate data on climate-related hazards, population vulnerability, forecast climate scenarios, sector-relevant data (water, health, agriculture, ecosystem), infrastructure and climate-related projects to support coordinated mid- to long-term adaptation planning aligned to global development goals. Specifically, it can help nations undertake the National Adaptation Planning (NAP) process. CSG uses the Early Warning, Early Action, Early Finance (AWARE) platform engine and benefits from the capabilities of the platform that are validated in the South Asian context.

description: Climate variability and its impacts on natural and human systems are increasingly visible across the globe. Despite international attention towards this so-called climate security nexus, understanding of how climate, conflict, and resilience interact is sparse. This is partly due to a lack of sources that combine relevant data. The aim of this concept is to develop a Climate Security Index (CSI) that will allow academics and policymakers to conduct evidence-based research into an imperative global challenge. The CSI would be able to produce an aggregate, comparable, subnational dataset that provides relevant information for academics and policymakers to analyze indicators across the nexus.

The FRESH initiative is developing an end-to-end approach to increase fruit and vegetable intake and in turn improve diet quality, nutrition and health outcomes while also improving livelihoods, empowering women and youth and mitigating negative environmental impacts. _x000D_
_x000D_
Worldwide intake of fruit and vegetables is too low contributing to poor quality diets and in turn, high prevalence of malnutrition and diet-related non-communicable diseases.​ Key barriers to increasing intake exist include the availability, accessibility, affordability and desirability of fruit and vegetables. The integrated end-to-end approach will address each key barriers by implementing co-located approaches that simultaneously address constraints to increasing the desirability, availability, affordability and accessibility of sustainable, safe and healthy produce and ultimately intake of fruits and vegetables, evaluating these approaches to help build evidence on what works and inform policy and program design.

description: Carbon credits can potentially be used in various ways to improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers. They may incentivize farmers to switch to crop management practices that reduce the carbon footprint and improve soil health and productivity in the long run. The compensation could be disbursed directly to farmers or be used to improve advisory or community services and cover the cost of inputs. Since their parcels and total land area are relatively small, the monetary value of carbon credits for a farm household is also small. Hence, it is essential for the Measurement, Reporting, and Verification tools to be cost-effective. To address the challenge, we designed a satellite remote sensing-based carbon offset estimation system to help smallholder farmers estimate carbon offsets from conservation agriculture practices using freely available datasets. We tested the proof-of-concept system in Bajío, Mexico. This report describes the data and approaches developed as an early-stage innovation.

description: Modern breeding is a data rich process, and requires data management software designed for the task of generating, tracking, storing and using the information produced by breeding programs for breeding decisions.  Many programs are currently not using a formal data management system; others are using older legacy systems.  With the Enterprise Breeding System becoming available, these programs can now adopt the new software.  Data migration into a new database is a complex process with many idiosyncrasies depending on how a breeding programs has been managing its data before adopting a new system, hence a clear and transparent strategy was needed.  Scope, process, and timelines will be defined so new adopters can quickly get value of the system. An important point of agreement for scope was the definition of a minimal set of operational data that would allow breeders to use the system within a year of beginning adoption.
